title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
layout_note: A left-to-right chain of framed vector states (Task Vectors -> Trimmed Task Vectors -> Aligned Values -> Merged Task Vector) with grey numbered operation boxes between them; from the trimmed vectors a branch drops to '(2) Elect Sign' and a small 'Sign Vector' panel, which climbs back up into Aligned Values from below. The states step up and down rather than sharing one baseline.
grouping: Each vector state is a black-outlined rounded panel with its name and symbol above it (τ, τ̂, γm, τm); operations are separate grey filled rounded boxes numbered (1)-(3). A legend without a frame fills the top-left corner.
shapes_depth: Flat. A task vector is a horizontal black axis with small white squares (parameters) and coloured vertical arrows up or down from each square (updates per model). Operation boxes are grey filled rounded rectangles; connectors are thick black arrows with right-angle elbows.
proposed_highlight: No element is marked as 'ours'; the three operations are the numbered grey boxes, and what each removes is shown in the vector panels: dotted 'redundant' arrows disappear after Trim, and minority-sign arrows become dotted in Aligned Values.
lesson: Draw every step of a parameter-level procedure on the same toy vector (five parameter squares with per-model up/down arrows) so trimming, sign election and merging show up as arrows vanishing, turning dotted or recolouring.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page footer ('37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)'). elements 'other' = parameter vectors drawn as stem-like arrows on an axis.

taxonomy.task: merging several fine-tuned models into one multitask model
taxonomy.note: family other: model merging; architecture other: no network drawn, only parameter vectors; depicts plots = per-parameter update arrows drawn on an axis like a stem plot

insights.structure: Vector states are framed panels and operations are small grey boxes between them, with the sign election as a lower branch that feeds back up into the aligned values.
insights.data: Each task vector is drawn as five parameter squares on an axis with a coloured arrow per model whose direction and length show the update's sign and magnitude.
insights.emphasis: The operations are emphasised only by numbering; the effect of each is the visible change in the arrows (dotted ones dropped by Trim, minority-sign ones dotted in Aligned Values, all green after Disjoint Merge).
insights.flow: Thick black arrows run left to right but turn right angles: up from Trimmed into Aligned Values, down and back up through Elect Sign, and down from Disjoint Merge into the merged vector.
insights.avoid: The main chain zigzags in height (Aligned Values sits above the other states, the sign branch below), and green means both the elected sign vector and the merged model.

arrangement.units: five black-outlined rounded panels, one per vector state, with grey numbered operation boxes between them; no enclosing frame
arrangement.inputs_as: a panel of three models' task vectors drawn as coloured up/down arrows on five parameter squares
arrangement.shared: the trimmed vectors feed both Aligned Values (up) and Elect Sign (down) through two elbow arrows from one panel

core.what: three numbered operations (Trim, Elect Sign, Disjoint Merge) between framed vector states, each state drawn as the same five-parameter axis so the effect of each stage is visible in its arrows

relations.form: framed vector panels left to right with grey numbered operation boxes '(1) Trim', '(2) Elect Sign', '(3) Disjoint Merge' between them
every state is a horizontal axis of five white parameter squares with coloured per-model arrows up or down, so trimming and sign conflicts are shown on the parameters themselves
the trimmed vectors (from the left) and the elected sign vector (from below) both enter the Aligned Values panel
Aligned Values -> Disjoint Merge -> Merged Task Vector continues right then turns down into the final panel

channels.colour: arrow colour = which model an update comes from (purple Model 1, pink Model 2, gold Model 3), green = merged model, keyed in the legend; the elected sign vector is also green, so green carries two meanings
channels.shape: white squares = parameters, coloured arrows = updates, grey filled rounded boxes = operations, black-outlined rounded panels = vector states
channels.line: solid arrows = influential values, dotted arrows = redundant or discarded values (keyed); thick black arrows = order of operations
channels.frame: one rounded black frame = one vector state, named with its symbol above or below

quality.strengths: the representations are drawn between the operations, as the same toy vector at each stage, so a reader sees what Trim removes and which arrows lose the sign vote; one keyed code each for model identity (colour) and kept vs discarded values (solid vs dotted); operations are compact grey boxes while the vector states get the space
quality.weaknesses: the chain changes height three times (up into Aligned Values, down to Elect Sign and back up, down into the merged vector), with right-angle elbows instead of one reading axis; green is used for both the elected sign and the merged model; the legend takes the top-left corner while the Aligned Values panel is pushed up to the top edge beside it

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
